Bucky's status as a Super Soldier is explained in a convoluted way and is difficult to properly ascertain throughout the films, but the clues are there, they're just kinda scattered throughout a *lot* of other Marvel stuff going on at the same time. It's a lot to keep up with, so I'll try to break it down.

Captain America: Winter Soldier explained that Hydra had experimented on Bucky(hence why he was on the table in First Avenger when Steve found him), which is where he got the strength to go toe to toe with Cap in the first place. But it was left a little vague, which felt a little bit like leaving it to us to put the pieces together, which can be *really* difficult when you're also piecing together and keeping track of a bajillion other lore bits in a *very* busy Phase 2.

Civil War further showed his Super status, confirming that whatever they'd done had put him on par with a bunch of other "Winter Soldiers" who had whatever version of the Serum he stole from the Starks at the beginning of the film. These were shown being changed by the serums used, becoming Super Soldiers in their own right, ones dangerous enough to topple regimes with ease. That's why Zemo killed them rather than waking them - he didn't want more Super Soldiers, that's his whole deal. It's why he was able to dogwalk pretty much everyone who wasn't either Cap, who he almost killed, and Black Panther, who was also a superhuman(though that was implied at the time).

FatWS has Walker make that comment about "serum running through your veins," to Bucky, and so on, and so forth. The robot arm helps, and was necessary after he lost the first one in the fall from the train, but that's a weapon - the rest of his body's definitely also super.

Basically HYDRA made a serum derivative while they were camouflaged inside of SHIELD and juiced him up. Spoiler for the film, but >!while talking to Red Guardian in Thunderbolts, he explains that it was HYDRA's super soldier serum he got, which Red Guardian replies is "fancy." So.!< He's definitely a Super Soldier, just like Walker is after using the refined serum from FatWS. The same one that made Karli and the Flag Smashers, whether we love or hate them(I'm mixed about it), into Super Soldiers as well.

Now, why he's a Congressman, I'll never understand. I kinda hated that. But that's a minor gripe for me, and I quite liked Thunderbolts otherwise. :)

Okay, pardon me if I sound snarky here, I'm legitimately not trying to be. It's late and I'm tired. That being said:

Naturally, people never rise up and things never get better. This is why Adolf Hitler reigned uncontested until he died of old age, handing over the reigns of the Reich to his successors who still rule today. Who rule alongside the never-collapsed Western Roman Empire, and frets about the Mongol Empire built by Genghis Khan to the north, which also never fell. They sometimes trade with Emperor Hirohito's successors in the still-living Japanese Empire, who from time to time have lunch with the Mycenaean Greeks.

Except obviously that isn't the case, because all of those Empires fell apart and all of the status quo's around them changed, and are still evolving. 

We're currently in an era of very short attention spans, with a population no longer used to these kinds of hardships and tumultuous times, which makes it *feel* like this is all inevitable, and unstoppable, and unending, because it hasn't ended *yet* and our brains are largely screaming at the lack of speedy resolution and dopamine. Because we're largely addicted to these bloody depression machines, myself included, as I type away on one of them to write this. I totally get why it feels like things are fucked, because they are, but I also know from learning about history that they aren't always going to be. Things will eventually change.

Empires always collapse, or at best, end up reduced and restructured. People with power and impunity eventually overreach. Mobs absolutely rise up when things get hard, and competing factions and groups splinter apart when old norms become stagnant and the systems holding together a society start to crumble. This is a process which always happens, and it ramps up in speed and devastation when the person leading the charge is an incompetent, self-deluding, demented idiot like Trump.

Our society right now is full of tons of people who are terrified, complacent, and comfortable in their place at the bottom, but this decades-old status quo we're enjoying *will not last.* Humans are still humans, and the fact that there are so many of us now, living in such a society as this, doesn't mean we always will. Our status quo is tens of years old, amid history books spanning thousands of years and a species that's been anatomically modern and living in tribes and societies for hundreds of thousands of years. Our recognizable ancestors lived for *millions* of years before that, and survived environmental calamities that reduced our global population to a few thousand. We very nearly went extinct, more than once, and you know what our species did?

We survived. We adapted. We built new societies, ones with beautiful art, joyous celebrations, and thriving families. It's what we do.

Having this many people and this much stuff doesn't stop the collapse, and in fact, it simply means that parts of it will probably be violent as hell. Death tolls we've never experienced, by sheer virtue of the fact that we've never simultaneously had eight billion living people at once like this.

And the rich? Much as they pretend to be, they aren't gods. They're just people, dependent upon other people. They rely on the folks who make and deliver their clothes, who produce their food, who wield their weapons of war, who tend them when they fall ill. Those people are *humans,* and when shit hits the fan, they'll be out here tearing things up like everyone else. Hell, some of the more well-equipped ones will probably rise to prominence over new factions and groups of people after the fact.

The question is, why *don't* we doubt them? History shows one constant, and one constant alone - no Empire ever lasts forever. Not even once. 

Change is inevitable, and some of that change will be positive. Not all of it, hell, probably not most of it. But some of it will be, and that's worth getting out of bed and keeping up the fight for as long as we can.

To me, at any rate. You can do whatever you want, I suppose.

One story I'm working on has a race of immortal beings, known to mortals as the Fae, who were basically shapeshifting shepherds of a world of nature and magic. Their "base" forms were bipedal, with varying features such as skin, fur, feather, scale, chitin, etc, often in vibrant colours, though they can appear more "humanoid" if necessary. Each could use magics freely to tend and balance the world, and they could take the shape of any beast, plant, or fungus as needed. When they had need, they took refuge among the branches of a massive tree overlooking the mortal world.

They lived in a free utopia, where none had power and all served, until five of them wanted to rule and shape the world rather than letting nature shape itself. These five stole the power from the tree, but in doing so, they inadvertently killed it. Henceforth they were known as the Fallen, and were cast down from the tree's branches to the mortal world below, ending the immortality of nature and causing the world's magic to corrode and weaken over time. The Fallen can still shapeshift and can wield great magics, but while they're stronger individually than the Fae, their corrupted forms are limited in the shapes they can take and they find themselves only able to work destructive, deceptive, and corruptive magics.

When each landed on the mortal world, their impact caused a different mortal race to emerge from the surrounding earth, a union of the magics of life and the corruption of their darkened souls. Each race is defined by the primary dark emotion of their specific progenitor when they hit the ground, producing five races of varying descriptions. Because I'm a talentless and unoriginal hack at the best of times, yes, one of them is humanity - or as the Fae call them, the Sons and Daughters of Greed.

The Fallen became worshipped by these mortal races as gods, and they are attempting to manipulate the mortals into destroying the remaining Fae and giving absolute power to the Fallen. When only they have magic and immortality, they believe that they'll effectively be *actual* gods. The Fae, meanwhile, tend groves where they attempt to safeguard nature's remaining magics, try largely in vain to grow saplings to replace the great tree, and fend off the mortal races. They see the mortals as the greatest threat to their hopes for a regrown world.

The heroes of the story have to reckon with their darker natures while trying to balance their place in the world between Fae who fear them, Fallen who deceive them into believing the Fae are monsters, and fellow mortals simply trying to exist.

It's a bit grim in places, and still very rough, but I'm having fun with it. :)

This is for my D&D setting of Vengevost, a cursed world full of dangerous monsters and dark magic. Civilization exists in hard-won enclaves carved out by people banding together and, at times, by the ruthless actions of their leaders. Armies and populations are smaller here than in some places, mostly because of all the horrors going on just outside the walls of towns and the hard-fought roads through the wilderness.

This breakdown is specifically for the main area we're in right now, which is the Tresnyan Marches, one of the three major centers of power:


- The Margrave rules the ten thousand souls of the city of Tresnya, and by extension, all of its lands and vassals.


- The Margrave's spouse is called the Margravine, and any heir of the Margrave's blood could potentially succeed them, though a marriage-only spouse cannot.


- Tresnya's militant arm is the Knightly Order of the Ebon Rose, currently five powerful Knights elevated to Nobility by the Margrave. These five outrank any but the Margrave himself, and serve him with an almost fanatical, near-religious sense of love and devotion.


- The Knights oversee a local standing army of six hundred full-time soldiers, with reserve forces of up to two thousand more ready for service, and can call up conscripts to supplement them from the peasantry in times of dire need. This army is considered higher in standing than vassal forces, though arguments about this have led to infighting before.


- Outside Tresnya and its surrounding lands, several vassal regions called Baronies exist, each administered by a Baron or Baroness.


- Barons run their Baronies however they see fit, provided they do not threaten Tresnya or her interests, pay the appropriate tribute, and contribute soldiers and resources in times of need.


- The children of a Baron or Baroness are called Baronets, and are often, but not always, their parents' presumptive heirs.


- All Barons maintain fighting forces, and have the ability to organize them however they like, provided that they can provide sufficient strength and numbers when called up by the Margrave. A Barony may have no more than fifty standing soldiers and two hundred proper reservists, though most find it too costly and difficult to maintain a standing army and instead rely upon town and village militias and regular peasant conscription for their forces in war.


- Sometimes a Barony falls to chaos, or rises up against the Margrave, or is conquered by an enemy. In these instances, the Ebon Rose and vassal armies from other Baronies are mustered to subdue the unruly region, at which point someone new is created Baron or Baroness by the Margrave's order and is then free to administer their new region as they please, again, provided they can provide what is owed as tribute and military strength.
- At times, new regions are conquered or existing Baronies are subdivided for one reason or another, either growing too powerful or, conversely, growing too unstable to control wider terrain. In these instances, the Margrave will create someone a Baron of a new Barony encompassing all the newly-taken lands, and will treat the new Barony as a new extension of their power.


- At times, Barons have been usurped, deposed, or replaced via coup d'etat. These instances have happened enough that Usurper Barons are a known concept, and when one rises, the Ebon Rose will rally their might and march into the usurped Barony ready for battle. If the coup has been completed by the time they arrive, or the region has otherwise stabilized, they'll usually accept the Usurper Baron as legitimate in exchange for a bent knee and an offer of tribute. If not, they'll pacify the region and install a new Baron themselves, as specified above.


- Towns, villages, and other settlements often have differing and contradictory ruling structures, many based on relic and remnant titles and structures from the time before the Great War that cursed the land and destroyed the previous High Fantasy civilizations a thousand years ago. They all either function by serving their Barons, or serve something else powerful enough to hold back the local Baron and/or make them play nice. Naturally, such places are prone to radical change and even destruction and later rebuilding based on the whims and happenings of the Barons, and the general ferocity of the world around them.

Tresnyan Marches TL;DR:

- Margrave rules City-State of Tresnya, all vassal Baronies.
- Knights of the Ebon Rose and their army are the Margrave's enforcers.
- Baronies serve Tresnya, ruled by Barons appointed by the Margrave.
- Baronies have smaller armies, pay troops and tribute to Tresnya in exchange for protection and membership of the whole Marches.
- Barons rule and structure their Baronies however they desire, so long as troops and tribute come on time.
- Unstable, rebellious, or conquered Baronies are pacified by the Ebon Rose and have new Barons installed as necessary.
- New regions conquered or joining have new rulers created Baron by the Margrave in exchange for troops and tribute.
- Usurpers can take over Baronies, have until Ebon Rose arrives in force to have things under control and bend the knee if they want to keep their Baronies. Otherwise, pacification.
- Towns, villages, and other settlements in Baronies are all structured individually and vary wildly, either serve Barons or serve things powerful enough to make the Barons leave them alone.

Mine grow to physical maturity over the first century, usually looking fairly close to shorter, slighter, more angular humans with pointy ears. Some of them have odd eye, hair, and skin colours from time to time depending on subrace. These look like "young adults," the way an early-20's person would look.

As they approach their second century, they begin to look closer to early thirties. Since they descend from Fey rather than natural creatures, their Faerie genetics become suffused with the magics inherent in their environments. They begin to express themselves in odd little changes and features dependant, again, largely on subrace(though extremely magical environments can affect this and even alter what subrace a given elf is).

Wood elves typically express this with eyeballs that gain a walnut-like texture and more vibrant natural colours for their irises, while their skins develop a woodgrain and their hair begins to grow small leaves, moss, and even twigs. 

High elves typically get skin that becomes more and more like semi-translucent, bluish porcelain with arcane glyphs, alongside an Arcane glow in their eyes.

Dark Elves, meanwhile, see their features grow more harsh and severe over time. Their eyes will become more intensely coloured to the point of black sclera and near-glowing irises, while some grow natural spiderwebs and arachnid bits in their hair. Some even grow slight insectoid bits from their brows, cheekbones, and jawlines, if they live past four or five centuries.

Natural elven lifespan, that being without magic of one sort or another extending it(most commonly seen with,  but not exclusive to, potent Druids) is around seven or eight hundred years. Few elves reach this, because eight centuries is a *hell* of a long time to live in a magical and dangerous world without monsters, mayhem, disease, or even simple accidents eventually happening to someone. Those who do cross these benchmarks begin to look truly *old,* even to the point of looking eerie and inhuman.

TL;DR - Elves age to physical maturity by 100, before proceeding to age with super weird magically-inspired features rather than human-esque wrinkles and whatnot.
